title: HashiCorp Relased Terraform Google Cloud Provider 8.0 in General Availability
gist: HashiCorp released Terraform Google Cloud provider 8.0 GA, a breaking release that switches default load balancing from Classic EXTERNAL to EXTERNAL_MANAGED, removes resources for retired Google services, and converts order-insensitive lists to sets; OpenTofu users can adopt most but lack the terraform query workflow.

insights.claim: Terraform Google provider 8.0 changes the default load_balancing_scheme for google_compute_backend_service and google_compute_global_forwarding_rule from EXTERNAL to EXTERNAL_MANAGED, so unset configs move from the Classic to the new external Application Load Balancer.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Risk of unintended changes to production load balancers for teams that don't pin the setting.
insights.locator: The most visible behavioral change affects

insights.claim: Provider 8.0 removes resources tied to retired Google Cloud services, including IAP brand/client, notebooks, ml_engine_model and BeyondCorp app connector resources, with replacements like Workbench, Security Gateway and Colab schedules.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Reflects Google Cloud's product consolidation and retirement cadence.

insights.claim: Order-insensitive attributes changed from lists to sets to prevent perpetual plan diffs when APIs return values in a different order.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Reduces operational noise in IaC pipelines.
insights.locator: On schema behavior, attributes where ordering

insights.claim: HashiCorp recommends upgrading to the latest 7.x release and clearing deprecation warnings before moving to 8.0, testing in non-production first.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Upgrade work is a recurring cost of IaC tool dependence.

insights.claim: Terraform's query/list-resource discovery workflow has no OpenTofu equivalent, with a tofu query feature request (issue #3787) still pending.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Feature divergence strengthens Terraform's differentiation against the open-source fork.

insights.claim: Write-only attributes in the provider require OpenTofu 1.11 or later, and OpenTofu's Resource Identity support was not confirmed at the time of writing.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: OpenTofu lags on some features, a consideration for enterprises choosing between forks.

insights.claim: The provider gained Terraform list resources for discovering infrastructure outside state across Compute Engine, IAM, BigQuery, Pub/Sub, Secret Manager and more, plus write-only attributes for secrets like AlloyDB passwords.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Import/discovery tooling lowers cost of bringing brownfield infra under IaC.
